mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises real interest rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) below 500k signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST < 500k for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below -1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls below -1% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in CPIAUCSL below 1% signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases risk appetite and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL < 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL < 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth above 0.5% monthly for three months) without a corresponding rise in consumption expenditures (GDPC1 flat) signals a savings-driven demand imbalance, which historically precedes equity market corrections and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat (change < 0.1%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS grows above 0.5% for three months while GDPC1 is flat.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS monthly change falling from >0.3% to <0% within two months) signals labor market cooling, which reduces wage pressure and supports corporate margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change transitions from >0.3% to <0% within two months
regime_hint: transition from tight to loose labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth decelerates from >0.3% to <0% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS growth above 0.4% monthly for four consecutive months) signals improving consumer demand, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS grows above 0.4% for four consecutive months.
